claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**How many children do you have that you'd like to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! I have one child I'd like to claim for - Alex, who's 17.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask a few more questions to determine your eligibility for Alex.

Since Alex is 17, an important factor is whether they are in approved education or training. **Is Alex currently in approved education or training?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex isn't in approved education at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Let me ask a follow-up question:

**Has Alex left education or training within the last 20 weeks and registered with either a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex hasn't done that - they just left school and haven't signed up with any careers service or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying. I have a few more questions to complete the assessment:

**Is Alex currently in paid work for 24 hours or more per week?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't work 24 hours or more per week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you. Let me ask one more important question:

**Is Alex currently receiving any benefits in their own right, such as Employment and Support Allowance or Universal Credit?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, Alex doesn't receive any benefits in their own name.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent

conversation.author: actor

conversation.author: eligibility_agent

Thank you. And finally:

**Does Alex currently live with you?**

conversation.author: actor

conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided, I'm afraid you are **not eligible** for Child Benefit for Alex.

Here's why:

While you normally qualify for Child Benefit for children under 16, Alex is 17 years old. For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit can continue if they are under 20 **and** they stay in approved education or training.

Since Alex is not currently in approved education or training, you don't meet this requirement. Additionally, Child Benefit can continue for 20 weeks if a 16 or 17-year-old leaves education and registers with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services, but Alex has not done this either.

If Alex's circumstances change - for example, if they return to approved education or training - you may become eligible at that point and could make a new claim.
